kasuya.overview: This HARIO teaching version divides the brew into five timed additions. The first two pours shape the balance, while the remaining three control strength; it is a clear starting point for learning pulse pouring.
kasuya.bestFor: Learning a structured, timed pulse routine

hoffmann.overview: A low-dose V60 built around measured additions, short pauses and gentle swirls. Its aim is to keep extraction even without relying on one long continuous pour.

rao.overview: A no-bypass Pulsar method that closes the valve for the bloom, then uses short additions after release. It shows how immersion time and pulse pouring can be separated.

licata.overview: A V60 sequence that moves from a forceful initial pour to a slow centre stream and a final turbulent addition. It is useful for practising pour speed and water-level control.

wong.overview: A Switch-based hybrid recipe that uses an open-valve first stage before closing the valve to steep. The clearly separated stages show how percolation and immersion can be combined.

boen.overview: A competition version with two controlled steeps and an open release. It is more detailed than a basic Switch recipe and depends on careful timing, valve handling and temperature.
boen.bestFor: Studying a technical competition Switch method

hoang.overview: A W60 recipe that combines a mesh bed with paper and three additions. The layered filter and sifting advice make preparation more involved while giving the brewer more control over fines and flow.

rojewska.overview: A compact V60 routine with a gentle circular pour followed by a fast centre pour. It is short and easy to read, but the quick timing leaves little room for hesitation.
rojewska.bestFor: A short V60 routine with a quick finish

grill.overview: A larger 30 g V60 recipe with a bloom, two pours and a three-minute target. It suits brewing more coffee at once and rewards a steady, simple pouring rhythm.
grill.bestFor: Brewing a larger cup or sharing

mallouhi.overview: A straightforward ratio-led V60 sequence: a measured circular bloom followed by one slower addition. Fewer stages make it approachable, though the source leaves temperature unspecified.
mallouhi.bestFor: A simple circular bloom and slow finish

chronicler.overview: A simple Switch standard that pours half the water with the valve open, then steeps the second half before release. It is an accessible introduction to the Switch's hybrid workflow.

kodama.overview: A competition ORIGAMI brew with four exchanges of agitation and a specific prep sequence. It is valuable for studying pour direction, bed movement and a controlled final flow.

kobayashi.overview: A competition ORIGAMI recipe that includes sifting, filter placement and a cooler final pour. Its strengths are precision and temperature control; the extra preparation is part of the method.
kobayashi.bestFor: Advanced ORIGAMI preparation and temperature control

selorio.overview: A timed four-pour ORIGAMI recipe with a specified grinder and CAFEC paper. It is useful when matching a documented competition setup closely because its pace and equipment are explicit.
selorio.bestFor: Recreating a documented grinder and paper combination

rincon.overview: A natural Geisha competition brew that changes water temperature across the pours. It is highly source-specific and illustrates how a recipe can respond to one coffee and water profile.
rincon.bestFor: Studying temperature changes for a specific natural coffee

gil.overview: A four-pour ORIGAMI method tied to a K-Ultra setting and Sibarist paper. It provides a concise timing structure for comparison, while equipment and bean-specific details remain limited.

hoffmann-ultimate.overview: A full 500 mL V60 recipe built around a 60 g bloom and two staged pours. The final stir and gentle swirl level the bed before drawdown; the source uses hotter water for lighter roasts.
hoffmann-ultimate.bestFor: A larger V60 brew with a clear timed structure

camber.overview: A 20 g V60 recipe shared by Camber Coffee at SCA 2023, with a 60 g bloom and pours to 200 g and 345 g. The source highlights anaerobic coffees and a 3:00–3:15 finish.
camber.bestFor: Brewing anaerobic coffees with a simple V60 sequence

lamill.overview: A one-pour Mugen recipe with no bloom, built around a single continuous pour and a long drawdown. It is a simple starting point for the restricted-flow dripper.
